On this page

Reflexes & Events ​

Reflexes are CRONs, but the trigger is an event instead of a clock.

Every producer — the run engine, webhooks, pollers, agents — reduces its raw payload to one normalized Event and hands it to emitEvent(). A Reflex rule fires when its source + type match and its match tree evaluates true.

Event → reflex → action flow ​

The Event ​

ts
interface Event {
  id: string;                          // unique — used for dedup / idempotency
  at: number;                          // epoch ms
  source: string;                      // 'run' | 'agent' | 'stripe' | 'github' | 'generic'
  type: string;                        // 'run.finished' | 'payment_intent.succeeded' | …
  actor?: string;                      // run title, sender handle, repo…
  payload: Record<string, unknown>;    // normalized, matchable fields
  raw?: unknown;                       // the untouched original, for audit / re-parse
  runId?: string;                      // set when the event originated inside a run
  depth?: number;                      // chain depth; the bus loop-guard caps it
  orgId?: string;                      // matching is scoped to same-org rules
}

The run producer ​

The first event source is the run lifecycle. It subscribes to the existing run-notice bus — the same one Telegram uses — so the run engine itself is not edited:

Run transitionEvent
donerun.finished
errorrun.failed
awaiting_input with a pending approval gaterun.needs_approval

Plain awaiting_input, paused, and cancelled emit nothing.

Matching ​

A reflex's match is a boolean tree, not a flat list:

ts
type MatchNode =
  | Condition
  | { all: MatchNode[] }
  | { any: MatchNode[] }
  | { not: MatchNode };

A leaf Condition is { field, op, value? }, where field is a dot-path into the payload (user.plan, amount, from).

OperatorNotes
eq neqStrict equality
gt gte lt lteNumbers only
betweenvalue is [min, max], inclusive
containsSubstring for strings, membership for arrays
startsWith endsWithStrings
matches / matchesIRegex, case-sensitive / insensitive; an invalid pattern fails closed
invalue is an array containing the field
existsNon-null, non-undefined
changedDiffers from the last value this reflex saw for this field; a first sighting counts as changed

changed is the one stateful operator — it keeps a small per-reflex-per-field memory, which is its entire point.

Actions ​

ts
type ActionSpec =
  | { kind: 'startRun' }
  | { kind: 'sendToRun'; runId: string }
  | { kind: 'notify' }
  | { kind: 'emitEvent'; event: { source, type, actor?, payload? } }
  | { kind: 'callAgent'; agent: string }
  | { kind: 'webhookOut'; url: string; method?: 'POST' | 'PUT'; headers?: Record<string, string> };

The brief is a template rendered per event, supporting {{payload.x}} and {{actor}} — so a fired run's prompt can quote the thing that triggered it.

emitEvent is what lets reflexes chain. The bus carries a depth and caps it, so a chain cannot run away.

Controls ​

FieldEffect
cooldownSecMinimum seconds between fires for this reflex
dedupKeyTemplate rendered per event; a repeated key within a TTL window is skipped
maxFiresAuto-disable after N total fires
requireApprovalPark the fire as a PendingReflexFire for you to approve or deny before the action runs
enabledThe kill switch
projectScope the fired run to a registry project

Fires act as the reflex's createdBy user — their budget and permissions govern the run that results.

The console ​

Every fire lands in the log as a ReflexFire with status fired, skipped, pending, denied, or error, plus the detail and the resulting runId. A separate RecentEvent feed shows what came across the bus and how many reflexes matched it — so "why didn't my reflex fire?" is answerable: either the event never arrived, or it arrived and matched nothing.

See also: Building a Reflex · Reflex Rules
